bulk.unit: Saved Samply on-CPU sample weight(count), not perf cycles or CPU microseconds

limits: Inclusive context intersections overlap; do not add them or subtract to estimate CPU costs.
Source/inline attribution is actual current431 per-address response; optimized/missing frames prevent an exhaustive partition.
Allocation/deallocation and Vec constructor contexts are sampled work, not allocator call counts, bytes or causality.
Receiver polling includes ready, pending and error checks; no wake/re-poll counts or blocked duration inferred.
No channels/outcomes removed; changing await order still requires failure/cancel contract review.
Capture lost2 bulk chunks and timestamp warning apply; no missing samples reconstructed.
Launch-to-exit scope includes warmup, verification, sorting and cleanup, not only throughput timer.
Inclusive shares overlap; native and inline representations are separate views and must not be added.
Sample-frequency normalization differs from raw perf-period cycle weighting; no cross-host CPU-rate comparison.
Unresolved frames are retained. Capture loss is preserved in original stderr and PROVENANCE.json; no missing samples reconstructed.
Thread labels do not identify leader/follower ownership; no leader-specific CPU attribution.
No browser used. All symbol queries used localhost Samply API with current frozen ELF plus original packed DWP.
Subset intersections are explicit; matches_state and compaction overlap and must not be summed.
fun_<hex> names identify FDE boundaries, not known semantic symbols; raw names remain unchanged.
Source/inline locations are per-address API results rather than coalesced sidecar chains.
Allocation/clone contexts are sampled stacks, not actual call counts or allocated bytes.
Capture loss and launch-to-exit scope from SUMMARY.json remain applicable.
Zero context count means no exact resolved frame observed; absent optimized inline symbols do not establish zero execution cost.
